subject: dirichlet transform example; monitoring convergence of non-identified variables

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: dirichlet transform example; monitoring convergence of non-identified variables
parts:
I just pushed a change to make the indices consistent
to Ben's last example before the Vectorization section
in programming.tex (currently page 73 in the 1.1.0 manual):

-------------------------
data {
int<lower=1> beta;
...
parameters {
vector[beta] z[K];
...
transformed parameters {
simplex[K] rho;
for (k in 1:K)
rho[k] <- dot_self(z[k]); // sum-of-squares
rho <- rho / sum(rho);
}
model {
for (k in 1:K)
z[k] ~ normal(0,1);
// implies: rho ~ dirichlet(0.5 * beta * ones)
------------------

I take it "ones" is meant to be a K-vector of 1 values?

Doesn't the dot_self introduce a multimodality in the
z posterior that could be overcome by constraining
z > 0? And the whole thing's going to be non-identified
anyway, so we have to be careful in monitoring convergence.

We should probably say something about convergence and
non-identified variables in the manual. Here, we can just
monitor the transformed simplex.

- Bob
